title: The two TH sounds
what: replacing /θ/ and /ð/ with /t/, /d/, /s/, /z/ or /f/ ('tink', 'dis', 'sink' for think)
summary: The unique tongue placement for 'th' sounds often leads to their substitution with more familiar phonemes, even for advanced speakers. This can subtly obscure meaning and affect perceived fluency.
listenFor: Actively monitor whether your tongue tip gently touches or slightly protrudes between your front teeth when producing 'th' sounds, rather than staying behind th

contrasts.note: The voiceless 'th' /θ/ is often replaced by /t/.
The voiced 'th' /ð/ is often replaced by /d/.

contrasts.wrong: I need to replace my sum drive.
contrasts.right: I need to replace my thumb drive.
contrasts.note: The voiceless 'th' /θ/ is sometimes replaced by /s/.
The voiced 'th' /ð/ is sometimes replaced by /z/.

contrasts.wrong: I'm not finking clearly on this matter.
contrasts.right: I'm not thinking clearly on this matter.
contrasts.note: The voiceless 'th' /θ/ is sometimes replaced by /f/.
The voiced 'th' /ð/ is sometimes replaced by /z/.
